paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: pride makes you forget who gave you everything. The ruler of Tyre got rich by wisdom and trading skill (Ezekiel 28:4-5), and then his heart said, "I am a god" (Ezekiel 28:2). God's answer is short: "Yet you are a man and not a god" (Ezekiel 28:2). Everything he had was a gift, and he acted like he was the one handing it out.

The lament shows how far pride can drop a person. The king of Tyre was "blameless in your ways—until wickedness was found in you" (Ezekiel 28:15). Then "Your heart grew proud of your beauty," and God cast him to the earth (Ezekiel 28:17). Baker, the gifts were never the problem. The trouble starts when we stare at the gift and stop looking at the Giver.

And look at the ending, because it's good news. God judges Sidon, and then He promises that Israel will "dwell securely, build houses, and plant vineyards" (Ezekiel 28:26). Over and over He says, "Then they will know that I am the LORD," and the last time it's "the LORD their God" (Ezekiel 28:26). So hold your gifts with open hands, friend, and let them point you to Him. The proud get brought down, but the people God gathers get a home and a God who is THEIRS.
